title: Ithaca municipal Flock offboarding request reconciliation
summary: Request #1899 advances the Ithaca termination timeline from the March 2026 council vote through the June 2026 hardware-removal gap while preserving uncertainty around vendor-confirmed shutdown, deletion, credentials, audits, sharing, and equipment custody.

data.question: What can public evidence establish about Ithaca's March 2026 Flock termination and subsequent shutdown/removal state?
data.method: Reconciled the existing canonical Ithaca targets with March 2026 termination reporting and June 2026 reporting quoting city officials about operational and physical-removal status.
data.framework: Council action, contract expiration, platform shutdown, credential access, data deletion, physical removal, equipment custody, and directed sharing are separate evidence states.
data.scope: Public municipal Flock termination and offboarding evidence for Ithaca; Cornell's separate campus network is not merged into the city network.
findings: Ithaca Common Council unanimously voted on March 4, 2026 to end the city's Flock Safety relationship; contemporaneous reporting identified 22 municipal cameras.
By June 3, five Flock camera units were still physically present downtown after the termination vote.

City official Alan Karasin told the Cornell Daily Sun the cameras were no longer operational to the city's knowledge, while the city was still awaiting confirmation from Flock that shutdown was complete.
The city said it waited for the contract to expire on May 23 and had no specified hardware-removal date at the time of the June 3 report.
conclusions: The municipal termination decision and later physical-removal gap are source-backed.
Continued physical presence is not evidence that the cameras remained operational or collecting data.
Vendor-confirmed shutdown, final deletion, credential revocation, audit preservation, equipment custody, and directed sharing remain unresolved.
recommendations: Recover the native March 4 resolution and implementation assignments plus the contract, amendments, invoices, and funding records.
Recover final Organization Audit, Network Audit, SharedNetworks, event logs, users/admins, deletion certificates, credential revocations, removal work orders, and equipment disposition records.
Test any claimed Ithaca Police to Cornell Police access edge only against native sharing/audit evidence.
counterarguments: The city's belief that cameras were offline was not yet confirmed by Flock in the June 3 report.
Hardware still standing after contract expiration could reflect removal scheduling rather than continued system operation.
limitations: No native city resolution, contract closeout file, or Flock platform export was recovered in this pass.
No serial-level 22-camera lifecycle inventory was recovered.
unresolved: When did Flock confirm platform shutdown, if at all?
Were all credentials and directed sharing edges revoked, and when?
What data deletion and audit-preservation actions occurred?
When and how was each camera physically removed or otherwise disposed?

data.research_question: What portion of request #1899 can be advanced now without duplicating existing Ithaca termination/offboarding identities?
data.method: Read the request and comments, searched current main for existing Ithaca targets, reused those stable IDs, and reconciled March 2026 termination reporting with June 2026 city-attributed operational/removal reporting.
classification_rules: Reuse stable canonical IDs when materially equivalent targets already exist.
Physical hardware presence does not establish platform operation or data collection.
City-attributed operational status is distinct from vendor-confirmed shutdown, deletion, credentials, audits, and equipment custody.
Cornell University Police and Ithaca Police remain separate networks absent a directed access edge.

findings.finding: Four existing canonical Ithaca targets cover termination compliance, deletion/offboarding, sharing history, and removal work orders and were reused.
March 4, 2026 termination and the 22-camera municipal scope are independently reported.
By June 3, five units remained physically present, while the city said they were no longer operational to its knowledge and awaited Flock confirmation.
Native offboarding, audit, deletion, credential, removal, custody, and sharing records remain unresolved.
